rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Hubble's law**, v = H₀d with H₀ ≈ 70 km s⁻¹/Mpc, makes every galaxy recede with speed proportional to distance — evidence that **space itself expands** (measured via redshift, z ≈ v/c). Running expansion backwards gives the **Big Bang** ~13.8 billion years ago: quarks and leptons in the first microsecond, nucleosynthesis of H and He by 3 minutes, and at 380,000 years the release of radiation that cools into…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **The Big Bang is an expansion OF space, not an explosion INTO space** — there is no centre.  ·  **The CMB is the Big Bang's afterglow**, cooled to 2.7 K over 13.8 billion years.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Expanding Universe Every distant galaxy recedes, and the farther it is, the faster it flees — Hubble's law. Run the film backwards and everything converges ~13.8 billion years ago: the **Big Bang**, whose echo still fills the sky as the cosmic microwave background.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Hubble's law Recession speed is proportional to distance: $$v = H_0 d \qquad H_0 ≈ 70 \text{ km s}^{-1}\text{/Mpc}$$ - Measured from galactic **redshift**: light stretched by expansion shifts to longer wavelengths; z = Δλ/λ ≈ v/c for small speeds.…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 115:** the Big Bang's first second produced the particle families. - **To Topic 117:** dark matter and dark energy dominate the universe's fate. - **To Doppler effect (Unit 4):** redshift is the same physics applied to light.
